title_en: You can ask the government for information
law: Right to Information Act, 2005, Sections 6, 7 and 19
rule_plain: You can ask a government office for information in writing or by electronic means. You do not have to say why you want it. The officer must answer within 30 days, or within 48 hours if it is about a person's life or liberty.
what_you_can_do: Send your request to the Public Information Officer of the office, with the fee that is set.
If you cannot write, the officer must help you put your spoken request in writing.
If you get no answer in time, or you are not happy with the answer, appeal within 30 days to an officer senior to the Public Information Officer in the same office.
After that, you can make a second appeal to the State Information Commission or the Central Information Commission within 90 days.
where_to_get_help: The Public Information Officer of the office; for a second appeal, the State Information Commission or the Central Information Commission.
